title: A Postcard for the Songbook
premise: Rafael Halloran, a ghostwriter who has spent a decade erasing herself from other people's stories, takes an anonymous pen-pal assignment through the Songbook Society, a letter-exchange club for writers. Her correspondent, 'Wren,' turns out to be Declan Osei—the rival memoirist whose book she is secretly writing under contract, and the man whose betrayal ended her career years ago. As their letters deepen into intimacy while their daytime rivalry sharpens, Rafael must choose between finishing the memoir that will secure her future and exposing the truth that could destroy them both. In the end she publishes the letters themselves as her own first book, forgives herself for the old betrayal that started everything, and chooses Declan—not because love conquers duty, but because honesty finally does.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's correspondence before turning to fiction. They write about people who hide in plain sight, and live quietly in a coastal town where they still answer every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She accepts a lucrative contract to ghostwrite rival memoirist Declan Osei's memoirs, telling herself the heart is trainable like any muscle. Flashback hints at a past betrayal between them. Emotional beat: armored self-containment masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Songbook Rules
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She joins the Songbook Society's anonymous pen-pal exchange for professional networking, swearing to keep it strictly transactional. She receives a first letter signed 'Wren'—wry, sharp, unsettlingly familiar. Beat: cautious curiosity.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Revealed: Declan is 'Wren,' assigned his enemy without knowing it, hoping anonymity might let him apologize for the incident that ruined Rafael's career. His opening letter is a disguised apology she misreads as mockery. Beat: guilt disguised as wit.

chapters.title: Interview Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Daytime: hostile memoir interviews where Declan deflects every personal question. Nighttime: letters where he confesses everything he won't say aloud. The dramatic irony tightens. Beat: vertigo of double intimacy.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. He recognizes Rafael's handwriting in the margins of his returned manuscript pages and nearly pieces together her identity as his correspondent—but convinces himself he's wrong. Beat: hope he refuses to trust.

chapters.title: The Found Family Table
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Sunday dinners with her chosen family—her landlady Odette, a retired typesetter, and Odette's foster kids—force Rafael to admit she's been hiding behind work. Odette warns: 'Invisible isn't safe, it's just slow.' Beat: warmth cracking armor.

chapters.title: Deadline Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The publisher moves the memoir deadline up; her advance—and her escape fund—is contingent on delivering a flattering manuscript. She begins cutting Declan's confessions from the draft. Beat: duty pressing on conscience.

chapters.title: Letters We Almost Sent
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. He drafts a confession naming himself as Wren, then burns it when Rafael coldly returns his revised chapters. Interleaved: the burned letter's text, more honest than anything in the memoir. Beat: cowardice and longing entangled.

chapters.title: Rain on the Archive Steps
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Trapped under an awning after a publishing event, they share an unguarded conversation about second chances—each speaking about the letters without knowing it. Beat: near-recognition, charged restraint.

chapters.title: The Old Betrayal
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Rafael's POV. Eight years ago, Rafael exposed Declan's mentor's plagiarism to save her own byline, believing it was integrity; it destroyed Declan's debut and made her the industry's invisible fixer. Beat: reckoning with the person in the mirror.

chapters.title: Wren Goes Silent
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Declan, convinced he's deceiving his correspondent, stops writing. Rafael discovers she misses him desperately—and realizes the feeling predates the letters. She writes anyway, unguardedly, for the first time. Beat: loneliness turned honest.

chapters.title: Odette's Drawer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Odette shows Rafael a drawer of fifty years of letters from her late husband, arguing that truth delayed is not truth denied—it's just heavier to carry. Rafael decides to finish the memoir with everything included. Beat: resolve kindled.

chapters.title: Chapter Thirteen of the Memoir
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Reading Rafael's new draft, Declan finds she has restored his confession about his mentor—including the part that implicates her own past testimony. He understands, finally, who she is and what she's carrying. Beat: stunned compassion.

chapters.title: Two Truths at Once
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. He confronts the publisher privately, threatening to kill the memoir unless Rafael gets full credit—or full release from the contract. The publisher counters with a legal threat that would bankrupt her. Beat: love against duty, declared.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the Songbook's annual reading, members read one letter aloud anonymously. Declan volunteers hers; the voice, the phrasing, the apology she finally hears plainly—she knows, and he watches her know. Beat: exposure as grace, not ruin.

chapters.title: Everything I Signed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. She delivers the complete, unflattering, true manuscript and terminates her contract, forfeiting the advance. The publisher threatens blacklisting; Odette's table catches her. Beat: costly integrity, held steady.

chapters.title: What You Forgive First
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Declan tells Rafael he forgave her years ago—that his anger was grief wearing armor—and asks what she must forgive herself for before she can accept it. Beat: the mirror, faced at last.

chapters.title: Blacklist Season
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The publisher's retaliation lands; contracts evaporate. Rafael drafts a proposal: publish the Songbook letters—both sides, names attached—as a book about loyalty, lies, and repair. Declan agrees, staking his reputation on hers. Beat: all-in gamble.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A small independent press releases 'A Postcard for the Songbook.' At the launch, they read their letters aloud together, the audience learning the whole architecture of deception and devotion. Beat: vulnerability made public, survived together.

chapters.title: Counteroffers
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The original publisher offers a lucrative deal to buy the letters and bury the plagiarism history. Rafael declines on behalf of them both; Declan backs her without hesitation this time. Beat: duty redefined as shared truth.

chapters.title: Postscript, Handwritten
chapters.summary: Declan's POV. Months later: quiet domesticity, Odette's table expanded by two, a new letter begun—not anonymous, addressed plainly. Declan writes the sentence he burned years ago and gives it to her in person. Beat: earned tenderness.

chapters.title: A Postcard for the Songbook
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, closing frame. Rafael mails a postcard to the Songbook Society resigning her membership—no longer needing strangers to practice honesty on. Final image: her heart, untrainable after all, beating visibly. Beat: wholeness, chosen and named.
